Bangladesh’s PFM framework runs from constitutional provisions through legislation to implementing rules and operational instruments. The order within the statutory tier below is for presentation; the cited assessment does not establish a hierarchy among those enactments.

1. Constitution of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh, Articles 81–92 — highest authority; establishes the basic financial procedures for managing public finances.
2. Public Money and Budget Management Act, 2009 — principal PFM statute; elaborates the constitutional procedures and defines core PFM elements.
3. Comptroller and Auditor General (Additional Functions) Act, 1974 — statute concerning audit of statutory public enterprises and local authorities.
4. Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty Act, 2012 — tax-revenue legislation.
5. Income Tax Ordinance, 1984 — income-tax legislation identified in the assessment; its cited amendment status is through July 2014.
6. Customs Act, 1969 — customs and tax-revenue legislation.
7. Public Procurement Act, 2006 — public-procurement legislation.
8. Financial, treasury, procurement and tax rules — lower-tier instruments, including the General Financial Rules, Treasury Rules, Subsidiary Rules, Public Procurement Rules, 2008, and VAT (Alternative Dispute Resolution) Rules.
9. Account Codes — accounting instruments identified separately from the financial rules.
10. Manuals and executive or administrative instruments — the Public Expenditure Management Manual, Internal Control Manual, executive orders, Statutory Regulatory Orders, and the Rules of Business and Allocation of Business, which address government procedures and institutional functions.

The assessment directly identifies the Constitution, the 2009 Act and several categories of implementing instruments. Treating the other named enactments as a statutory tier above rules, and grouping the operational instruments below them, follows their legal form; a finer ranking among individual statutes, rules, codes, manuals and orders is not established by the cited passage.
